constraints: Each selected index is stable across every descriptor for that unit or aircraft.
The two index choices are independent diagnostic axes, not a claim that either is a general rule.
Exactly two complete return blocks and two priority-list lines with one blank continuation each are required; no coalesced or extra diagnostics.

events: ID0 ready+ in TEACH-UNIT at BASE-01
ID1 ready+ in TEACH-UNIT-2 at BASE-01
ID0 allocated from TEACH-UNIT then ready-
ID1 allocated from TEACH-UNIT-2 then ready-
preparation start/end for each ID with no resource wait
joint mission start with IDs0,1 and duration2
two return blocks, either whole-block order

partial_order: h0 ready before h7 allocation; exactly one aircraft remains tied to each explicit unit.
h7 allocation precedes preparation; preparation precedes h8 joint start; h8.5 task start precedes h9.5 task completion.
h10 mission success precedes completion; each ID's turnround start precedes its own complete return block.
Return blocks may commute as units are distinct; lines within each block may not reorder or interleave.
reject: grouped ready counts replacing one per unit
interpretation_limit: This finite eight-arm parser can support only the bounded two-unit shared-base mission behavior. It does not establish general station-controller indexing or return ordering.

primary_expected.basis: Accepted A03 one-unit same-base and A17 distinct-base logs both render station/controller index0 and ID0 then ID1; this is a predeclared hypothesis, not an established two-unit/shared-base law.

other_seven_finite_forms.purpose: Preserve and classify a controller/index/order surprise without changing the oracle after observation. A separate contract would be required to accept any such branch.
